links.outcome: Multiple-choice accuracy of LLMs with versus without retrieved context from UK public health guidance
links.effect: Retrieved context substantially increased multiple-choice accuracy across diverse LLMs; smaller open-weight models with retrieval matched or outperformed larger models without retrieval. Gains were driven by retrieval quality and context selection.
links.quote: Providing retrieved context substantially increases multiple-choice accuracy across a diverse set of LLMs, enabling smaller open-weight models to match or outperform larger models used without retrieval, with gains primarily driven by retrieval quality and careful context selection.

unlisted_practices: Using hybrid (dense plus sparse) retrieval to improve recall and ranking in RAG systems
Rubric-based LLM-as-a-judge for free-form answers, validated against dual human annotations

screen.reason: Evaluates RAG (retrieval-augmented grounding vs ungrounded LLMs) across various configurations to mitigate hallucinations in public health question answering.
